title: Weight Sharing Reduces Parameters
subject: Neural Networks
statement: Convolution ties weights across positions, reducing parameters versus a fully connected layer.
long: Reuse one filter everywhere. It encodes stationarity of features.

title: Convolution Is Translation Equivariant
subject: Neural Networks
statement: Shifting the input shifts a convolutional feature map by the same amount up to boundaries.
short: Shift the image, shift the features.
long: Shift the image, shift the features. The same filter applies everywhere.

title: Pooling Operation
subject: Neural Networks
statement: Pooling replaces a local region by a summary such as maximum or average.
long: Downsample feature maps. Max pooling gives local tolerance.
proof: Partition into regions and reduce each.

title: Recurrent Neural Network
subject: Neural Networks
statement: An RNN applies the same transition at each time step while carrying a hidden state.
short: A loop lets the network remember.
long: A loop lets the network remember. Weights are tied across time.

title: Backpropagation Through Time
subject: Neural Networks
statement: BPTT unrolls a recurrent network over time and backpropagates on the resulting graph.
long: Unroll then backpropagate. Long sequences make a deep graph.
proof: Apply the chain rule along time.

title: Vanishing Gradients in Long Sequences
subject: Neural Networks
statement: Repeated multiplication by the same Jacobian can make gradients decay exponentially with sequence length.
short: Old information is hard to learn.
long: Old information is hard to learn. Exploding gradients are the companion issue.
proof: Multiply Jacobians along the unrolled path.

title: LSTM Gating
subject: Neural Networks
statement: LSTM uses input forget and output gates plus a cell state to control information flow.
long: Gates decide what to remember. The cell has an additive gradient path.

title: Gated Recurrent Unit
subject: Neural Networks
statement: GRU simplifies LSTM with reset and update gates and no separate cell state.
long: A lighter gated cell. The update gate interpolates states.

title: Transformer Block
subject: Neural Networks
statement: The transformer replaces recurrence with stacked self attention and feedforward blocks.
long: Attention is the core operation. It parallelizes across positions.
proof: Stack attention and feedforward with residual links.

title: Scaled Dot Product Attention
subject: Neural Networks
statement: Attention computes weighted averages of values using softmax of scaled query key products.
long: Softmax over similarities gives weights. Scaling avoids saturation.

title: Multi Head Attention
subject: Neural Networks
statement: Multi head attention runs several attention functions in parallel on different projections.
long: Different heads learn different relations. It is an architectural design choice.

title: Positional Encoding
subject: Neural Networks
statement: Positional encodings inject order information into permutation invariant attention.
long: Add position signals to embeddings. Without them attention sees a bag of tokens.

title: Self Attention Has Quadratic Cost
subject: Neural Networks
statement: Full attention over n tokens computes an n by n score matrix.
long: Long contexts are expensive. Sparse and linear variants try to help.

title: Residual Connections
subject: Neural Networks
statement: Residual blocks add the input to a transformed version of itself.
long: Layers learn perturbations of identity. They create direct gradient paths.

title: Residuals Ease Optimization
subject: Neural Networks
statement: Identity skip paths give gradients a direct route through deep networks.
long: Gradients have an identity highway. Empirically supported with theoretical analyses.

title: Batch Normalization
subject: Neural Networks
statement: Batch normalization standardizes activations using batch statistics and learned scale and shift.
long: Normalize within mini batches. Inference uses running statistics.
proof: Compute batch moments and affine transform.

title: Layer Normalization
subject: Neural Networks
statement: Layer normalization standardizes across features per example independently of the batch.
long: Normalize per example. Works well in transformers.

title: Dropout
subject: Neural Networks
statement: Dropout randomly zeroes activations during training and scales the rest.
long: Randomly drop units in training. Full network is used at test time.

title: Dropout as Approximate Averaging
subject: Neural Networks
statement: Dropout approximately averages many thinned networks with exact equivalence only for linear models.
short: It behaves like an ensemble heuristic.
long: It behaves like an ensemble heuristic. Expectations match only in simple cases.

title: Weight Decay
subject: Neural Networks
statement: Weight decay shrinks parameters each step and equals L2 regularization for plain SGD.
long: Penalize large weights during optimization. With adaptive optimizers equivalence can break.

title: Autoencoder
subject: Neural Networks
statement: An autoencoder learns an identity map through a bottleneck representation.
long: Compress then reconstruct. The bottleneck forces compression.

title: Variational Autoencoder
subject: Neural Networks
statement: A VAE learns probabilistic encoder and decoder by maximizing the ELBO with a latent prior.
latex: \mathcal L=\mathbb{E}_{q(z\mid x)}[\log p(x\mid z)]-D_{KL}(q(z\mid x)\parallel p(z))
long: Autoencoder with variational prior. The KL term regularizes the latent space.
proof: Apply variational inference with amortized encoder.

title: Reparameterization Trick
subject: Neural Networks
statement: Gaussian latent samples can be written as a deterministic function of fixed noise, permitting backpropagation.
long: Move randomness outside the network. Gives low variance pathwise gradients.

title: GAN Minimax Objective
subject: Neural Networks
statement: A GAN trains a generator and discriminator in a two player game.
short: A forger and detector improve together.
long: A forger and detector improve together. At equilibrium distributions match in ideal settings.

title: GAN Training Instability
subject: Neural Networks
statement: GAN optimization can oscillate or collapse because it is a game not a single objective.
long: Training can fail despite capacity. Empirical observation with partial theory.
